confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from five web searches. They mostly returned aggregator and crowd-sourced indexes (Numbeo-style mirrors, Expatistan, CityCost updated Oct 2026) plus 2026 travel guides. I could not open Numbeo directly. Sources differ in date and venue type, and harbour-front prices run well above neighbourhood tavernas. Euro prices were converted at roughly 1.16 USD per EUR, an approximate general-knowledge rate that I did not search. Meals and coffee are best supported (about EUR 15 inexpensive meal, about EUR 50-55 mid-range for two, about EUR 3.5 cappuccino). Beer (about EUR 4.5) rests on index figures of about EUR 4.0, nudged up for 2026 and July tourist weighting. Cocktail (about EUR 10.5) and wine glass (about EUR 6) have thin direct evidence: one low-reliability EUR 9 cocktail figure and blog ranges of EUR 9-13 and EUR 6-10. They are therefore anchored at about 2.3x and 1.3x the beer price. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July peak season and were not checked against live listings. The RBA rate comes from a single search result reporting the RBA daily figure for 2026-11-18.
comparable_city_reasoning: Comparable to other Greek tourist towns such as Rethymno and Heraklion, with harbour-front venues priced closer to Athens' tourist core. Accommodation reflects July peak-season levels for a popular Cretan resort town.
